chapter: Learning from Fletcher's circle in New York
title: Practicing on Fletcher's piano; Hawkins' patience and not revealing secrets
summary: Horace corrected his wrong chords at Fletcher's piano. Hawkins never embarrassed players for mistakes, and told Tommy Dorsey's men he didn't know how the notes came out so they wouldn't steal his ideas.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: After you'd hear those things from him or the various people that were talking in those sessions, would you go off on your own and practice some of those things. Did you have that opportunity, you know to --

I didn't have too much. The only thing -- I was more or less concentrating on playing the right chords, and I'd know if I'd make a few klinkers, I'd go home and I'd straighten them out on this particular piano that we're lookin' at right now, which was Fletcher's piano.
You had this piano or did -- this was Fletcher's piano in New York.

New York City, and I would go home and practice on this thing, and there was certain chords that -- I would take me a pencil, you know, and mark the mistakes, that I would make, but the fella would you know, the klinkers (inaudible) and keep on playin', you know? This is one thing about Coleman Hawkins. Even though you did something wrong, he would tell you to continue or keep playin'. Even on certain record sessions I was in, he had some personnel in there that actually, he could have done better. He was a patient guy, though, you know? But he never would reprimand you so that you'd be embarrassed, super genius, (inaudible). And he would always help you. You could ask him things, you know. But yet I, on the other hand, I've seen guys come up to him, like out of Tommy Dorsey's band in those days. They'd come up to Hawk, and they'd say, 'Man, how

did you make so and so?" And Hawk would look all silly, he'd say, "I don't know. The notes are there, they just come out. But he knew. Where other guys would take time and show these guys, and the next thing you know these guys (unintelligible)
Yeah. They'd use it, and they'd play places where you'd never play. Hawk was smart, he'd tell 'em, I don't know. The notes, just there. They just seem to come out. He knew.
